query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Powder‐pack boriding treatment applied to boride-based components will significantly improve their resistance to molten aluminum corrosion relative to untreated components by forming a protective surface boride layer.
generation.material_initial_state: Boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment without any additional surface treatment.
generation.intervention: Application of a powder‐pack boriding process to create a controlled, protective surface layer of borides.
generation.conditions: High temperature conditions typical of hot-dip aluminum plating, where the components are exposed to molten aluminum under operational exposure times.
generation.structural_mediator: A protective layer of surface borides formed during the powder‐pack boriding process.
generation.mechanism: The powder‐pack boriding creates a dense, adherent boride layer that acts as a barrier, impeding the diffusion and reaction of molten aluminum with the underlying material, thereby reducing corrosion.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated components will exhibit substantially lower corrosion rates (as indicated by reduced mass loss and less surface degradation) in molten aluminum compared to untreated samples.
generation.baseline: Performance of untreated boride-based components under the same molten aluminum exposure conditions.
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of the protective boride layer should remain under the high temperatures and exposure durations characteristic of hot-dip aluminum plating; performance may vary with variations in process parameters and alloy compositions.
generation.uncertainty: While preliminary literature suggests improvements, the exact magnitude and long-term stability of the protective layer under cyclic operational conditions remain to be validated.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of boride-based components: one group receives the powder‐pack boriding treatment and the other remains untreated. Expose both sets to controlled molten aluminum baths at representative plating temperatures for a fixed period. Assess corrosion resistance post-exposure through mass loss measurements, microscopic surface analyses, and depth profiling.
measurements: Surface morphology via scanning electron microscopy (SEM)
Chemical composition analysis (e.g., EDS) to verify the presence and integrity of the boride layer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated components do not show a statistically significant reduction in mass loss, surface degradation, and/or support the presence of a continuous protective boride layer compared to untreated components, then the hypothesis is falsified.

chosen.approach: Powder‐pack boriding to create protective surface borides
